research_scope: Independent Wave2 source-free review of shared mathematical prerequisites with original context and non-merge restrictions.

aliases.reason: The convex-set source uses a two-point convex combination tx+(1−t)y for t∈[0,1], which is an instance of the finite convex-combination construction in the convex-hull source. Terms with zero weights can be removed or replaced by a single coefficient 1; positivity convention and arity are specialized, not new operations.

Both normal-extension formulations use the same polynomial splitting condition: over a field extension, a nonzero polynomial is a scalar multiple of linear factors, with multiplicities. One ranges over irreducibles with roots and the other over element minimal polynomials; normality itself stays parent-level.

A countable union of pairwise disjoint members used in an equivalent sigma-algebra axiom is a countable indexed union of sets, exactly the prerequisite used in the ordinary sigma-algebra formulation. Pairwise-disjointness and closure under that union are separate source-specific conditions.

The outer-measure codomain record and the general nonnegative-measure codomain record denote the same extended nonnegative reals [0,+∞], with infinity included and standard extended addition/order. Countable subadditivity versus additivity is a parent distinction.

The category localization source requests invertibility of a morphism, defined by existence of an inverse g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y. This is precisely the categorical-isomorphism prerequisite already used in groupoids; universal localization is a distinct parent.
